In all, 40 Walkers started, including 25 of our members, a promising start for the new season. In the absence of Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen led the field, followed by Bob Readman and Smith of the Police.
(Clayton, Readman, East, Churcher.) 73 points.
Sawyer Memorial Cup: 1st, McMullen, 15 mins. 6.6 secs; 2nd Readman, 15.25; 3rd, East, 15.42. Discus.—Powell Trophy: 1st, Bergvalds, 123 ft. 8½ ins.; 2nd, J.
Churcher, McMullen, East, Readman.

Backed up by Bert East, Bob Readman and Bert Clayton, we once again succeeded in winning the scratch team race. The race marked the return of Jack Rutland to racing after a long break, and although he was fairly well down the field, it was pleasing to see him out once again.
Team Championship.—3rd Cadogan A.C., 45 points. Readman, 5; Rutland, 10; Oliver, 14; Bentley, 16.
Warr who is improving quickly, but the hero of the day was Bob Readman who although feeling the effects of the National Police Championship two days previously battled to the finish to score for us.
All our lads started fairly steady and at three miles Charlie Churcher and Bob McMullen were in 5th and 6th positions, whilst Bob Readman and George Oliver were together at 15th.

The individual titles have also been won by our walkers, viz., Readman, Readman and Bidgood respectively. Mick Porter finished 5th in the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon Race on Easter Monday, which was run in very bad weather conditions.
Dave McMullen retained his 2 miles walk title with A. Readman second and G.
Handicap Team Race: 1, Belgrave H. “C,” 203 mins. (Tebbutt, McGreechan, Jarlett, Warr); 3, Belgrave H. “A,” 207.54 (McMullen, James, Readman, Bidgood).

Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakeley and Readman, closely followed by Sapcote, Sutton and Robins.

This was matched by Readman's 5th place in the 7 mile track walk behind Roland Hardy's British record. Our only other performance of note on the main day was from Bill Lucas, who always timed his best performances for championships.
